title: Capture a journey as stable walkthrough modules

fields.outcome: A developer can capture an authorized browser journey as deterministic, stable walkthrough modules without writing Playwright code for that journey.
fields.scope: Implement a capture library for the ST-01 fixture contract that authenticates through environment-backed values, executes the profile journey, records actions/routes/observed API calls, and writes a schema-valid manifest. Exclude annotation rendering, source-code ownership mapping, change invalidation, DOM replay, and video.
fields.acceptance: Given the agreed fixture contract and journey definition, capture produces a deterministic schema-valid manifest with stable module and step IDs and no secret values.
fields.decisions: Own files under src/capture and capture-specific tests. Develop against the route and API contract in docs/contracts/mvp-interfaces.md; use a test double or data URL when ST-01 is unavailable. Do not modify shared schemas or package metadata; report integration changes instead.
fields.verification: Run capture twice against equivalent fixture state, validate both manifests, compare stable identities, assert observed routes and requests, and scan output for supplied secret values.
fields.dependencies: The contract defined by st-01 and the existing walkthrough schema and Playwright dependency.
fields.risks: Browser timing and generated identifiers can make output nondeterministic; request observation alone does not prove backend ownership.

criteria.expectation: Capture accepts a base URL, journey goal, and environment-variable names for authorized credentials.
Capture performs login and the profile update journey using stable user-visible controls.
The result contains stable module and step IDs that remain unchanged across equivalent runs.
The manifest records actions, routes, and observed login/profile API endpoints without claiming unobserved ownership.
The generated walkthrough validates against schemas/walkthrough.schema.json.
Generated files and diagnostics do not contain credential values, cookies, tokens, or storage state.
A failed step identifies the module, step, and observable cause without exposing secrets.
